```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

required_packages <- c("ggplot2", "GGally")
for (pkg in required_packages) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(pkg, repos = "https://cran.rstudio.com/")
  }
}
library(ggplot2)
library(GGally)
```

## Q1: Load the dataset and identify numerical / categorical variables

```{r q1}
df <- read.csv("HepatitisCdata.csv", row.names = 1)

df$Category <- as.factor(df$Category)
df$Sex      <- as.factor(df$Sex)

str(df)
summary(df)

cat_vars <- names(df)[sapply(df, is.factor)]
num_vars <- names(df)[sapply(df, is.numeric)]

cat("Q1 Categorical Variables:", cat_vars, "\n")
cat("Q1 Numerical Variables:", num_vars, "\n")
```

## Q2: Scatter plot - two numerical variables (X, Y) + one variable as color

```{r q2}
p2 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = ALB, y = ALP, color = Category)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Q2: ALB vs ALP colored by Category") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p2)
```

## Q3: Scatter plot - two numerical variables + color + shape (4 variables)

```{r q3}
p3 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = ALB, y = ALP, color = Category, shape = Sex)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(title = "Q3: ALB vs ALP by Category (color) and Sex (shape)") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p3)
```

## Q4: Scatter plot - two numerical variables + color + point size (4 variables)

```{r q4}
p4 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = ALB, y = ALP, color = Category, size = Age)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(title = "Q4: ALB vs ALP by Category (color) and Age (size)") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p4)
```

## Q5: Bubble plot - three numerical variables (X, Y, bubble size)

```{r q5}
p5 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = ALB, y = ALP, size = AST)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "steelblue") +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1, 10)) +
  labs(title = "Q5: Bubble plot - ALB vs ALP, size = AST") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p5)
```

## Q6: Subplots using facet_wrap()

```{r q6}
p6 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = ALB, y = ALP)) +
  geom_point(color = "darkgreen") +
  facet_wrap(~ Category) +
  labs(title = "Q6: ALB vs ALP faceted by Category") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p6)
```

## Q7: Subplots using facet_grid() with two categorical variables

```{r q7}
p7 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = ALB, y = ALP)) +
  geom_point(color = "purple") +
  facet_grid(Sex ~ Category) +
  labs(title = "Q7: ALB vs ALP faceted by Sex (rows) and Category (columns)") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p7)
```

## Q8: Pairs plot - at least four numerical variables

```{r q8, fig.width=7, fig.height=7}
numerical_vars <- na.omit(df[, c("ALB", "ALP", "ALT", "AST")])

pairs(numerical_vars,
      main = "Q8 Pairs Plot: ALB, ALP, ALT, AST",
      pch = 19,
      col = "darkblue")
```

## Q9: Parallel coordinate plot - at least four numerical variables, differentiated by category

```{r q9}
df9 <- df[complete.cases(df[, c("ALB", "ALP", "ALT", "AST", "Category")]), ]

p9 <- ggparcoord(df9,
                  columns = c(which(names(df9) == "ALB"),
                              which(names(df9) == "ALP"),
                              which(names(df9) == "ALT"),
                              which(names(df9) == "AST")),
                  groupColumn = "Category",
                  scale = "std",
                  order = "anyClass",
                  alphaLines = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Q9: Parallel Coordinate Plot - ALB, ALP, ALT, AST by Category") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p9)
```
